note: Typed tool signatures for the state solver. Atoms: see atoms[]; entity atoms apply per entity. from_inputs: output atom <- source input slot (pass-through). makes_true: the tool sets the atom from its prompt, settings or model. not_specified: no guarantee; no solver credit. dropped: input atoms whose output atom is not_specified (PRD rule; atoms replaced from another slot are not listed). For video and image outputs, from_inputs + makes_true + not_specified cover every atom in scope. inputs[] lists media and prompt slots; numeric and enum params are in settings_that_set_atoms. basis: documented/inferred per magic-hour-tools.json maintains/mutates; mixed = both. Added tools carry a provider field; their specs are by design, not from docs.

atoms.definition: Who the entity is: face and recognizable likeness (for a product or logo: its brand identity).
Hair and head shape outside the face.
Body build, skin and proportions.
Clothing and accessories the entity wears.
Facial expression and eye gaze.
Body and head pose, and the motion or action over time.
Mouth motion matches the speech_audio track.
Voice timbre and speaking manner of the entity.
Setting and environment behind the entities.
Light direction, quality and colour on the scene.
Objects in the scene that are not entities or wardrobe.
Framing, shot size, angle and camera motion.
Visual rendering: art style, palette, colour grade.
On-screen text and graphic overlays: captions, titles, logos.
Spoken-word audio: words, language, timing.
Music track.
Sound effects and ambient sound.
Output media: image, video, audio or data.
Length in seconds.
Aspect ratio.
Pixel dimensions.
Frames per second.

signatures.notes: First frame = input image [inferred]; end frame [documented]; motion and camera from prompt [documented]. Identity can drift in later frames [inferred]. aspect follows input image [inferred]. audio=true adds model audio with no content control, so no layer atom gets credit.

Maintains nothing. Without references, the prompt sets identity only for a described generic entity; a real person needs a reference image. references semantics undocumented. Cross-call consistency not guaranteed. audio=true gives uncontrolled audio.

Likeness kept in realistic mode [documented]; prompted mode lowers likeness and lets the prompt change background and camera [documented]. Background, framing and audio pass-through [inferred]. Needs a clear frontal face. No text input: make speech with AI Voice Generator first.

assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Lip motion [documented]. Video content kept and audio replaced [inferred]. The input voice comes with the audio and can mismatch the person's identity. Best with one frontal speaker; audio and video of similar length.

assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Face identity, expression, head motion, lighting [documented]. Body, pose, background, camera, audio [inferred]. head_hair stays from the video, so a full likeness may need Character Replace. voice stays from the video. individual-faces needs Face Detection first. v2 keeps identity better.

assets.youtube_url can replace the video file. Motion and structure [documented]; framing and camera [inferred]. Repaints every frame: text may break, identity detail may drift [inferred]. Audio pass-through undocumented: mux the source audio back. Not for content changes.

Changes objects, colours, scene details, style named in the prompt [documented]. Credit only for the atoms the prompt names; atoms the prompt does not name carry from the video [inferred]. One edit per call. Generative re-render: text and audio pass-through not guaranteed.
Only spoken language is documented. Visuals, identity, voice timbre and lip re-sync are inferred and unverified (no tool guide page). On-screen text is kept but not translated. 1-30 s clips.

assets.youtube_url can replace the audio file. Start image = first frame only [documented]; content morphs over time, so image atoms get no credit across the clip. Style and camera from presets [documented]. Audio kept as the track [inferred]; audio must cover end_seconds. Morphing look, not photoreal motion.

Timing follows audio [documented]; reference image = initial frame [documented]. Audio kept in output [inferred, unverified]. Lip sync to speech is not documented. Without an image, entity atoms come from the prompt with no identity guarantee. Prompt conflicting with the image degrades output.

Signature is for style.mode=replace. Scene, background, motion kept [documented]; character appearance from image [documented]. speech_sync from video [inferred]. Audio pass-through undocumented. Pick the person with point selection when many people.

animate.notes: Motion from the video moves the character image.

signatures.notes: Adds burned-in captions from a transcript of the video's speech_audio [documented]. Existing text and all other atoms kept [inferred]. No language parameter; no SRT export; noise and music reduce accuracy.

Maintains nothing. Identity only for a described generic entity; not consistent across calls [inferred]. Some style.tool presets (logo, poster, thumbnail) render text, but text is not in the spec, so no text credit.

signatures.notes: General editor. Credit only for the atoms the prompt names; atoms the prompt does not name carry from image_file_paths[0] [inferred]. Can compose atoms from extra reference images [documented]. Identity can drift [inferred]. aspect_ratio=auto follows input. Text is not in the spec, so text carries and gets no credit. One edit per call.
Face identity, expression, lighting [documented]. Pose, body, hair, background [inferred]. Output resolution is plan-capped. head_hair stays from the target: use Head Swap for hair.
Body, pose, scene kept [documented]. Whole head with face and hair from head image [documented]. expression from head image and text from body image [inferred].
Scene and person appearance kept [documented]. Pose can adapt to the scene [inferred], so pose_action is the tool's own. Lighting from scene [inferred].

from_inputs.wardrobe: assets.garment_file_path (region per garment_type; other regions from person)

signatures.notes: Pose, lighting, background [documented]; face identity [inferred]. Crossed arms and busy backgrounds degrade.
Keeps facial identity only [documented]. Sets background, attire, lighting, framing [documented]. Needs exactly one face. Hair and expression not specified.
Expression, gaze, head pose by sliders [documented]. Identity, lighting [documented]; background, clothing [inferred]. pose_action here = head pose only. Large slider values look unnatural.
Content and composition kept [documented]; aspect [inferred]. creative mode can reinterpret detail and style. Weak on text-heavy images.

Subject cutout [documented]; dimensions kept [inferred]. No relight: subject lighting can mismatch the new background. props and text in the old background are lost; a held prop counts as subject only when the cutout keeps it. Fine hair and low contrast degrade.
Adds colour (style: palette) [documented]. Content and structure kept [inferred].
No image input; no duration control [documented]. Output is gif, mp4 or webm (an image project). No audio.
Template image is fixed by preset [documented]; the tool writes panel text for the topic [documented]. Visual atoms come from the template preset, not the user's assets.
text here = encoded payload, not readable glyphs. Scannability is a goal; test it. Busy styles can break scanning.
Script text kept as the words [documented]. voice from a preset only; a real person's voice needs AI Voice Cloner. No language parameter; duration follows text length. Not in hosted MCP.
Timbre, intonation, speaking patterns from the sample [documented]; new words from the prompt [documented]. Sample: one clean speaker, >= 3 s. Not in hosted MCP.

Changes opacity of a layer or the whole frame over time. No atom covers opacity or visibility timing: open gap in the vocabulary.
On the whole frame it sets framing (camera). On an overlay layer it sets text placement. Pixels otherwise pass through.

signatures.notes: Join in time. duration = sum of segment durations (minus transition overlap). Each segment keeps all its atoms in its own time range; the solver splits a goal into per-scene sub-goals and joins them here. Segments must share aspect, resolution, frame_rate, or a crop_reformat runs first.

Join in layers. Each layer keeps the atoms of its own input; the solver splits a goal into visual, speech, music and sfx sub-goals and joins them here. speech_sync holds only when the speech slot is the same audio the video was lip-synced to. Mix only (no video) gives an audio output.
